title: a numeric literal that evaluates to Infinity is refused inside a durable value, because a Plan cannot persist it and a replay would resume with a different number

diagnostics.messageContains: non-finite numeric literal is not durable

notes: specification/durable-execution.mdx §Durable Boundary Contract: 'Every value crossing an Action or Flow persistence boundary MUST satisfy the compiler-checked durable codec contract.' Infinity has no JSON encoding — JSON.stringify(Infinity) is the string 'null' — so a Plan that accepted this literal would persist a null where the author wrote a number and a replay would resume from a different value than the first run computed, silently, with nothing thrown. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: SMITHERS4111 is enforced by both implementations and, until this case, was declared by NOTHING. It was not always so. Step 11 withdrew the durable branch and loop WALLS and rewrote the 17-durable cases that declared them into acceptances asserting Flow.manifest; four codes lost every declaration they had that way (SMITHERS4106, 4111, 4112, 4124) while the rules themselves stayed in both backends. That is the bucket COVERAGE.md's second subtraction exists to count, reached from the unusual direction: not a rule shipped without a case, but a case retired off a rule that is still there. THIS IS NOT THE RULE THE OLD CASES DECLARED. The withdrawn SMITHERS4111 was WALL 5, the fallthrough for 'an expression the Plan cannot name', and it is gone — both implementations now throw PlanUnrepresentable there and the Flow publishes an Effect Manifest instead (see typeof-on-a-durable-input-is-rejected, which keeps its old name and is an `expect: output` case today). What survived is the set of durable-VALUE sites, and both implementations say so in the same words at the withdrawal: 'The other SMITHERS4111 sites — a non-finite literal, a spread, a duplicate field, an array hole, a computed projection key — are durable-VALUE rules, not walls, and stay' (poc/src/durable/source-compiler.ts:1595, compiler/forkbridge/durable.go.txt:1241). This case declares one of those five. THE DECLARED POSITION: 17:28 is the literal `1e999` itself, not the Action call and not the arrow function — a value rule points at the value. Both backends report the same code, the same position and the same sentence, so no marker is needed and Backend agreement is 1/1. WHY THE SHARP SPELLING: `1e999` is a legal TypeScript numeric literal that the checker accepts without comment, so no assignability diagnostic fires first and the refusal has to come from the durable value codec. `Infinity` as a bare identifier would not do: it is a host global and would be refused by a different rule in a different family. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed — the evidence is in this revision's report: the report site was deleted from the reference and this case turned red; the declared code and the declared column were each mutated and the case turned red on BOTH backends; the file was restored and sha256-compared byte-identical after every mutation.
